title: The held world with nothing growing in it
question: You asked that the world not start with any seeds — this is what she walks out into now. Does the bare land read as somewhere worth planting, or just as an empty map?
context_md:
Your playtest item: *"The world should not start with any seeds. The druid has her own seeds to plant and that populates the world."*

This is the real app at frame 3, nothing sown yet. The whole change was three zeroed densities in the `druid` worldgen preset — the pass that scattered life already knew how to do nothing.

The other half of the item is on the readout: **SEED MOSS x8**. Her supply used to be infinite. It is now a pouch of 8 of each kind, spent when she sows, refused out loud when empty, and refilled only by standing in a wood she grew.

The question I cannot answer from here is whether an *empty* world is the right starting point or whether it wants something — a few survivors, a dead stand — to plant against.

items.label: bare, as generated
